title: Visualizing On-Target Drug Binding in Mammalian Tissue Using Tissue Clearing and Click Chemistry
author: Pang, Ye

steps.title: Prepare tilted tube rack
steps.instruction: Set up a tilted rack for click reactions using two 2 mL Eppendorf tubes.

substeps.instruction: Remove caps from two 2 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Attach the uncapped tubes to an autoclavable 4‑way test‑tube rack with tape so the rack is tilted, allowing maximal agitation in a small reaction volume.

steps.title: Administer PF7845‑yne intraperitoneally
steps.instruction: Inject 1 mg kg⁻¹ PF7845‑yne dissolved in 10 % DMSO, 2 % Tween‑80 in saline (0.1 mg mL⁻¹) at a volume equal to 1 % of mouse body weight.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 mg mL⁻¹ PF7845‑yne solution in the stated vehicle.
For a 20 g mouse, inject 200 µL using an insulin syringe.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse 1 h after drug injection with 5 % v/v isoflurane in air (alternative: 100 mg kg⁻¹ ketamine + 16 mg kg⁻¹ xylazine).

steps.title: Perfuse with ice‑cold PBS
steps.instruction: Clear blood by perfusing ice‑cold PBS through the circulatory system at 10 mL min⁻¹.

substeps.instruction: Place pump tubing in ice‑cold PBS (or 4 % PFA) and connect to a 26G needle.
Turn on the pump to fill the tubing.
Open the chest and make a small incision at the right atrium to let venous blood exit.
Insert the needle into the left ventricle.
Perfuse PBS at 10 mL min⁻¹ for ~2 min (≈20 mL) until the liver is clear and outflow is transparent.

steps.title: Perfuse with ice‑cold 4 % PFA
steps.instruction: Fix tissue by perfusing ice‑cold 4 % PFA at 10 mL min⁻¹ for 2 min until the body becomes stiff.

substeps.instruction: Observe body twitching, tail flicking, and head movement as signs of successful fixation.

steps.title: Decapitate and dissect brain
steps.instruction: Remove the brain and place it in 4 % PFA overnight at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Decapitate the mouse with tough‑cut surgical scissors.
Cut skin along the midline and pull aside to expose the skull.
Make two lateral cuts underneath the brainstem.
Cut the skull along the midline over the cerebellum.
Insert scissors near the eyes and sever the skull.
Cut the skull along the midline over the cortex to fully expose the brain.
Use thumb and index finger to pull the skull away; peel off remaining bone with forceps.
Remove the brain and immerse it in 4 % PFA at 4 °C for overnight fixation.

steps.title: Wash brain in PBS
steps.instruction: Drain excess PFA and wash the brain in PBS for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Embed tissue in agarose
steps.instruction: Embed the brain in 2 % agarose and let it solidify at 4 °C for 1–2 h.

steps.title: Section brain at 100 µm
steps.instruction: Cut the agarose‑embedded brain into 100‑µm coronal or sagittal sections using a Leica VT1000S (or similar) vibratome.

steps.title: Store sections in PBS‑NaN₃
steps.instruction: Place sections in PBS‑NaN₃ storage buffer and keep at 4 °C (can be stored for 1–2 months; discard if buffer becomes cloudy).
